topics.title: Quiet / Noisy places

questions.text: Do you like quiet or noisy places?
questions.answer: I prefer quiet places because I can focus better. In a quiet environment, I feel calm and relaxed. Noisy streets make me tired and sometimes give me a headache. That’s why I usually choose quiet places for study or rest.

questions.text: Would you like to go to quiet or noisy places on weekends when you are free?
questions.answer: I usually go to quiet places on weekends, like a park or a small café. They help me relax after work and spend free time peacefully. Sometimes I go to crowded restaurants with friends, but most of the time I enjoy peaceful weekends.

topics.title: Art

questions.text: Do you like art?
questions.answer: Yes, I like art because it shows beauty and feelings. When I see a painting or sculpture, I can feel the artist’s emotions. Art also gives me new ideas and makes life more interesting.

questions.text: Do you like visiting art galleries?
questions.answer: Yes, I enjoy visiting art galleries because I can see many different works. It is a good way to learn about history and culture. Walking in a gallery also makes me feel calm.

questions.text: Do you want to be an artist?
questions.answer: No, I don’t want to be an artist because I don’t have the talent. But I admire artists for their creative work. They can bring beauty and imagination to people’s lives.

questions.text: Do you like modern art or traditional art?
questions.answer: I prefer traditional art because it connects me to history and culture. Modern art is sometimes too difficult for me to understand. Traditional art is easier and more enjoyable.

topics.title: Shoes

questions.text: Do you like buying shoes?
questions.answer: Yes, I like buying shoes because they are both useful and stylish. A new pair can make me feel confident and happy. Shoes also show a little of my personal style.

questions.text: Have you ever bought shoes online?
questions.answer: Yes, I have bought shoes online many times. It is convenient and saves me time. But sometimes the size is not right, so I prefer to try them in a shop.

questions.text: How much money do you usually spend on shoes?
questions.answer: I usually spend around 300 to 500 yuan on shoes. If the shoes are good quality, I don’t mind paying more. I think comfortable shoes are always worth the money.

questions.text: Which do you prefer, fashionable shoes or comfortable shoes?
questions.answer: I prefer comfortable shoes because I walk a lot every day. Fashionable shoes may look nice, but sometimes they hurt my feet. Comfort is always more important than style for me.

topics.title: Plants

questions.text: Do you keep plants at home?
questions.answer: Yeah, I do! I have a couple of small plants on my desk and a bigger one in the living room. They make the place feel fresher and more welcoming.

questions.text: What plant did you grow when you were young?
questions.answer: When I was a kid, I grew some sunflowers in the backyard. They grew really tall, and I remember feeling proud when they finally bloomed. It was a fun little project.

questions.text: Do you know anything about growing a plant?
questions.answer: I know a little bit, like making sure the plant gets enough sunlight and water. It’s also important not to overwater it. Other than that, I just try to keep it healthy.

questions.text: Do Chinese people send plants as a gift to other people?
questions.answer: Yes, they do. People often give plants like orchids or lucky bamboo because they symbolize good fortune. It’s a thoughtful gift, especially for new homes or business openings.

topics.title: Working with old people

questions.text: Have you ever worked with old people?
questions.answer: Yes, I have. Back in school, I volunteered at a community center and helped some older people with daily activities. It was a nice experience because I learned a lot from their stories.

questions.text: Are you happy to work with people who are older than you?
questions.answer: Yes, I don’t mind at all. Older colleagues usually have more experience, and I can pick up useful skills from them. I think it makes the teamwork stronger.

questions.text: What are the advantages of working with old people?
questions.answer: One advantage is that they usually have more patience and knowledge. They can guide younger people and help solve problems more calmly. Working with them often feels reassuring.

topics.title: Dothing sth well

questions.text: Do you have an experience that you did something well?
questions.answer: Yes, I remember once I gave a class presentation and it went really smoothly. I felt confident and my classmates seemed interested. It gave me a real sense of achievement.

questions.text: Do you have an experience that your teacher thought you did a good job?
questions.answer: Yes, my teacher once praised me for writing a clear and well-structured essay. She said I explained my ideas in a simple way. That made me feel really encouraged.

questions.text: Do you often tell your freinds when they do something well?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I think it’s important to cheer for your friends when they achieve something. A few kind words can make them feel proud and motivated.

topics.title: Rules

questions.text: Are there any rules for students at your school?
questions.answer: Yeah, there are a few basic rules at my school—like we’ve gotta show up to class on time every morning, cause if you’re late too often, you might get a warning from the teacher. We also can’t eat or drink in the classrooms, only in the cafeteria—they say it helps keep the learning space neat.

questions.text: Do you think students would benefit more from rules?
questions.answer: Yeah, I definitely think students get more benefits from rules—they help keep things organized, so we don’t end up in chaos, and they also teach us to stick to a routine, which is super useful for later life. Without clear rules, it’d be easy for people to skip homework or disrupt classes, so having them actually creates a fair environment where everyone can focus on learning without distractions.

questions.text: Do you have a teacher who does his/her job very well?
questions.answer: Yeah, definitely—my math teacher is awesome at her job; she always breaks down tough concepts into simple parts so even students who struggle with math can keep up, and she’s super patient when we ask questions.She also goes the extra mile to help us outside class, like staying after school to review tricky topics—you can tell she really cares about our progress, which makes everyone want to work harder.

topics.title: Public places

questions.text: Have you ever talked with someone you don’t know in public places?
questions.answer: Yeah, I have—once I was waiting for the bus on a rainy day, and an older lady next to me struck up a conversation about the weather; we ended up chatting for 10 minutes, and it made the wait feel way shorter.Another time, I had to ask a stranger in a café to pass me the sugar since it was on their side of the table, and we even exchanged a few words about how busy the place was that morning.

questions.text: Do you wear headphones in public places?
questions.answer: Yeah, I usually wear headphones when I’m out in public—like on the subway or walking to class—because they help me drown out the noise and let me focus on my music or podcasts.I don’t crank the volume up too high, though; I make sure I can still hear a bit of what’s going on around me, just so I don’t zone out completely and miss things like my subway stop.

topics.title: Carrying things

questions.text: What do you often carry with you?
questions.answer: Yeah, I always carry a few essentials with me—my phone, wallet, and a reusable water bottle, ‘cause I hate having to run out to buy drinks when I’m out and about, especially on hot days.I also throw a small notebook and pen in my bag, just in case I need to jot down a quick note—like a friend’s address or a reminder for homework—since my phone battery sometimes dies unexpectedly.

questions.text: What do you do if your item is heavy?
questions.answer: I’ll usually switch up how I carry it first—like if it’s a heavy bag, I’ll alternate shoulders every few minutes so one side doesn’t get sore, or I’ll hold it with both hands to spread out the weight a bit.If it’s really too heavy, I’ll look for a place to set it down for a minute—like a bench or a sidewalk ledge—to take a quick break, instead of trying to lug it around nonstop and tire myself out.

topics.title: Going out

questions.text: Do you bring good or snacks with you when going out?
questions.answer: I usually do bring some snacks with me when I go out—stuff like granola bars or fruit, ‘cause I often get hungry halfway through the day, and it saves me from having to grab expensive snacks on the go.Sometimes if I’m meeting friends for a walk or a trip to the park, I’ll also pack a small bag of chips or cookies to share—nothing too big, just enough to tide us over until we can get a proper meal later.

questions.text: Do you always take your mobile phone with you when going out?
questions.answer: I definitely always take my phone with me when I go out—It’s a total must-have, honestly. I use it for everything, like checking maps if I get lost, paying for coffee, or even texting friends to meet up somewhere, so I’d feel super stuck without it.The only time I might forget it is if I’m in a huge rush, but even then, I usually realize pretty quickly and end up doubling back home to grab it—losing or forgetting my phone feels like leaving part of myself behind!

topics.title: Borrowing & lending things

questions.text: How you you feel when people don’t return things they borrowed from you?
questions.answer: I usually feel a bit annoyed and let down when people don’t return borrowed things—especially if it’s something I use often, like my favorite notebook or a charger, because it messes up my daily routine. I try not to make a big deal out of it at first, but it does make me think twice about lending them things again later.

questions.text: Do you like to lend things to others?
questions.answer: I don’t mind lending things to others, especially close friends or family who I know will take care of them—like a book or a kitchen tool, since it feels good to help someone out when they need it. But I’m a bit cautious about lending valuable or irreplaceable items, just because I’d be gutted if something got lost or broken.

questions.text: Have you ever borrowed money from others?
questions.answer: I have, but only once—last year when I forgot my wallet while out shopping, so I borrowed a small amount from my roommate to pay for groceries. I made sure to pay her back the next day because I hate owing people money, and I didn’t want her to think I was unreliable.

topics.title: Museum

questions.text: Do you think museums are important?
questions.answer: I definitely think museums are super important—they’re like treasure troves of history and culture, letting people get up close to artifacts and stories that you can’t just learn from a textbook. They also help keep traditions alive, especially for younger generations who might not otherwise get a chance to connect with their heritage or the wider world’s past.

questions.text: Do you often visit museums?
questions.answer: I don’t visit museums super often—maybe once every few months—usually when there’s a new exhibition that catches my eye, like a photography show or a history exhibit about a period I’m curious about. I tend to go with friends or family too, since chatting about what we see makes the visit more fun than going alone.

questions.text: When was the last time you visited a museum?
questions.answer: The last time I visited a museum was about two months ago—my cousin was in town, so we went to the local art museum together to check out its new exhibition on modern paintings. I spent around two hours there, and I even picked up a small souvenir from the gift shop to remember the day, since some of the artworks were really impressive.

topics.title: Advertisement

questions.text: Do you see a lot of advertising on trains or other transport?
questions.answer: Yes, I often see many ads when I take the train or bus. They are usually about food, clothes, or mobile phones. Sometimes the ads are very colorful, so they catch my attention. But after a while, they feel a bit boring. Still, they are everywhere in public transport.

questions.text: Do you like commercials?
questions.answer: Honestly, I don’t really like commercials. Many of them are too long and repeat again and again. Sometimes they interrupt my favorite TV shows, which is annoying. But if the commercial is funny, I don’t mind watching it. I prefer short and creative ones.

questions.text: What kind of advertising do you like?
questions.answer: I like advertising that tells a story. For example, some ads show family love or friendship. They are warm and make me remember the brand. I also like ads with good music, because the song stays in my head. These ads are more meaningful.

questions.text: Is there an adverttisement that made an impression on you when you were a kid?
questions.answer: Yes, when I was a kid, I saw a milk advertisement on TV. It showed happy children drinking milk and playing outside. The music was very cheerful, and I remembered the slogan clearly. At that time, it made me want to drink milk every day. Even now I still remember it.

topics.title: Crowded places

questions.text: Do you like crowded places?
questions.answer: No, I don’t like crowded places very much. They are usually noisy and stressful. When there are too many people, it’s hard to move around. I also feel tired after staying in a crowd. That’s why I prefer quiet places.

questions.text: Is the city where you live crowded?
questions.answer: Yes, the city where I live is quite crowded. There are many cars on the road every day. During rush hour, the streets are full of people and buses. Sometimes it takes a long time to travel even a short distance. So, yes, it is very crowded.

questions.text: Is there a crowded place near where you live?
questions.answer: Yes, near my home there is a big shopping mall. On weekends, it is always full of people. Families go there to shop, eat, and watch movies. The parking lot is also crowded with cars. It is the busiest place in my area.

questions.text: When was the last time you were in a crowded place?
questions.answer: The last time I was in a crowded place was last month. I went to a concert with my friends. The stadium was packed with people and very noisy. We had to wait in line for a long time to get in. It was fun but also tiring.

topics.title: Chattting

questions.text: Do you like chatting with friends?
questions.answer: Yes, I really enjoy chatting with friends. It makes me feel relaxed and happy. We often share our daily stories and laugh together. Chatting also helps us understand each other better. For me, it’s an important part of friendship.

questions.text: What do you usually chat about with friends?
questions.answer: We usually chat about school, work, and hobbies. Sometimes we talk about movies or music we like. We also share our problems and give advice to each other. It’s nice to have someone to listen. Chatting makes our friendship stronger.

questions.text: Do you prefer to chat with a group of people or with only one friend?
questions.answer: I prefer to chat with only one friend. In a group, it is sometimes too noisy and I can’t say much. With one friend, I feel more comfortable and honest. It is easier to listen and understand. So I like small talks better.

questions.text: Do you argue with friends?
questions.answer: Sometimes I argue with friends, but not often. Most of the time we understand each other well. If we have different opinions, we try to talk calmly. After a short time, we usually make peace. I think real friends don’t stay angry for long.

topics.title: Having a break

questions.text: What do you usually do during a break?
questions.answer: During a break, I usually drink water or have a snack. Sometimes I check my phone for messages. If I have more time, I take a short walk. These small activities help me relax. After that, I can work better.

questions.text: What do you like to do during a break?
questions.answer: I like to listen to music during a break. It helps me forget stress for a while. Sometimes I chat with classmates or colleagues. A short talk can make me feel happy. Breaks give me energy to continue my work.

questions.text: Hos often do you take a break?
questions.answer: I usually take a short break every one or two hours. If I study or work for too long, I lose focus. A break helps me to stay fresh and clear-minded. It’s important not to work nonstop. Regular breaks improve my efficiency.

questions.text: Do you take a nap when you have a rest?
questions.answer: Yes, I often take a short nap when I have a rest. Even 15 or 20 minutes makes me feel much better. After a nap, I have more energy to continue working. But I try not to sleep too long. Otherwise, I feel lazy and slow.

topics.title: Sharing

questions.text: Did your parents teach you to share when you were a child?
questions.answer: Yes, my parents often taught me to share toys and snacks with my cousins and friends. They told me that sharing makes people happier and brings us closer. I think this habit helped me learn kindness and cooperation from an early age.

questions.text: What kinds of things do you like to share with others?
questions.answer: I like to share food, such as fruit or homemade dishes, with my friends. Sometimes I also share books or study materials with classmates. I think sharing knowledge and experiences is just as valuable as sharing things.

questions.text: Do you have anyting to share with others recently?
questions.answer: Yes, recently I bought some snacks during a trip, and I shared them with my colleagues. I also found a useful English learning app, and I recommended it to my classmates. Sharing makes me feel more connected to others.

questions.text: Who is the first person you would like to share good news with?
questions.answer: The first person I usually share good news with is my best friend. She always listens carefully and celebrates with me. Sometimes I also tell my parents, because I know they will be proud of me.

topics.title: Growing vegetables / fruits

questions.text: Are you interested in growing vegetables and fruits?
questions.answer: Yes, I’m quite interested in it. I think it’s a healthy and relaxing activity. Growing vegetables gives me fresh food and also teaches me patience. It’s a good way to spend time outdoors.

questions.text: Is growing vegetables popular in your country?
questions.answer: Yes, it is popular, especially in the countryside. Many families have small gardens where they grow vegetables or fruits. In cities, some people also try balcony gardening. It’s becoming more common nowadays.

questions.text: Do you think it's easy to grow vegetables?
questions.answer: I think it’s not very easy, because it needs time and care. You have to water the plants regularly and protect them from insects. But if you learn the basic skills, it can become easier and enjoyable.

questions.text: Should schools teach students how to grow vegetables?
questions.answer: Yes, I think schools should teach this. It helps students understand where food comes from. It can also teach responsibility and teamwork when they grow plants together. It’s a useful life skill for the future.

topics.title: Friends

questions.text: Do you have a friend you have known for a long time?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I’ve known my best friend since primary school, and we’ve stayed close ever since. We don’t see each other every day, but whenever we meet, it feels like nothing has changed.

questions.text: What do you usually do with your friends?
questions.answer: I usually hang out with my friends at cafés or watch movies together. Sometimes we just chat about daily life and share funny stories. It’s always relaxing and enjoyable.

questions.text: Where do you often meet your friends?
questions.answer: Most of the time, I meet my friends at a shopping mall because it’s convenient for everyone. We grab some food and walk around together. Sometimes we go to someone’s home if we want a quieter place.

questions.text: Do you often go out with your friends?
questions.answer: Yes, quite often. We like to go out on weekends, either to try new restaurants or just explore the city. It’s a great way to relax after a busy week.

questions.text: How important are friends to you?
questions.answer: Friends are really important to me. They give me support when I feel down and celebrate with me when I achieve something. Life would feel boring without them.

questions.text: Do you prefer to spend time with one friend or with a group of friends?
questions.answer: I prefer spending time with one close friend because the conversation feels more personal. In a group, it can be fun, but sometimes it gets a bit noisy. One-on-one talks are more meaningful for me.

questions.text: Would you invite friends to your home?
questions.answer: Yes, sometimes I do. It’s cozy to stay at home together, maybe cook a simple meal and chat in a relaxed way. I think it feels warmer than just meeting outside.

questions.text: Is there a difference between where you meet friends now and where you used to meet them in the past?
questions.answer: Yes, there is. In the past, I usually met friends at school or near my neighborhood. Now I prefer cafés or shopping malls, because it’s more convenient and comfortable.

questions.text: Why are some places suitable for meeting while others are not?
questions.answer: I think it depends on the atmosphere. A café or park is suitable because it’s quiet enough to talk. But noisy or crowded places make it hard to have a good conversation.

part3.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of family business?
part3.answer: One advantage of a family business is trust. Family members usually share the same goals and values, so they can work closely together. Another benefit is long-term stability, because they want to pass the business to the next generation. However, there are also disadvantages. Conflicts may happen when family members disagree on money or management. Sometimes emotions make decision-making less professional. So a family business needs clear rules.

part3.text: Is it good to work with family members?
part3.answer: Working with family members can be good because you feel supported. You don’t have to worry too much about trust. However, it can also be stressful, because work problems may hurt personal relationships. For example, if you argue about business, it’s hard to separate it from family life. So I think it depends on how people manage the balance.

part3.text: What kinds of family businesses are common in your country?
part3.answer: In my country, small shops and restaurants are very common family businesses. Many families run small grocery stores, bakeries, or noodle restaurants. Some also run clothing shops or small hotels. These businesses are not very large, but they provide stable income and support family life. They also create a strong sense of community because customers often know the owners well.

topics.answer: I would like to talk about my uncle, who runs a small bakery in my hometown. He started this family business about fifteen years ago, and now it has become one of the most popular bakeries in our area. The shop mainly sells bread, cakes, and some traditional local snacks. Every morning, you can smell the fresh bread from far away, and many people line up before the shop opens. My uncle is not only the boss but also the main baker. He wakes up at four o’clock every day to prepare the dough. His wife helps him manage the cash and customer service, and their son takes care of online orders and delivery. I think the teamwork makes the bakery very successful. From him, I have learned the importance of hard work and patience. He told me that at the beginning, the business was very small, and sometimes they even lost money. But he never gave up. He kept improving the taste of his bread, listened to customer feedback, and slowly built a good reputation. Now the bakery is well known, and they even have loyal customers from nearby towns. What impressed me most is his attitude towards quality. He always says, “People trust us with their food, so we must give them the best.” This simple sentence has taught me that honesty and responsibility are more important than quick success. I believe his family business is not only about selling bread, but also about building trust and sharing happiness with the community.

part3.text: Do you think it's better for children to have a few close friends or many casual friends?
part3.answer: I think it’s better for children to have a few close friends. Close friends give real support and help build trust. Many casual friends can make life fun, but they don’t provide the same deep connection. Children need someone they can share secrets with and rely on. Quality is more important than quantity in friendship.

part3.text: Do you think a child's relationship with friends can be replaced by that with other people, like prents or other family members?
part3.answer: I don’t think so. Parents and family give love and care, but friendship is different. With friends, children learn how to share, argue, and solve problems as equals. These skills are important for social life. Family love is important, but it cannot replace the unique role of friends.

topics.answer: I would like to talk about my best friend, Lisa. She is the same age as me, and we first met in high school. We sat next to each other in English class, and we quickly became close friends. At that time, we often helped each other with homework and shared snacks during the break. Over the years, our friendship has grown even stronger. I have known Lisa for more than ten years now. Even though we study and work in different cities, we keep in touch almost every day. We usually chat online, and we meet up at least twice a year. Whenever I face problems, she is always the first person I call. Lisa is important to me because she understands me deeply. She listens patiently when I need to talk and gives me honest advice. She also supports my dreams, even when others doubt me. For example, when I decided to prepare for the IELTS exam, she encouraged me to keep studying. Without her support, I might have given up halfway. What I value most about her is loyalty. She never talks behind my back, and I can trust her completely. She has taught me that true friendship is not about how often you meet, but how much you care for each other. I feel very lucky to have such a friend in my life.

part3.text: What kind of music is popular in your country?
part3.answer: In my country, pop music is the most popular. Young people like songs by famous local singers and international artists. Traditional folk music is also loved, especially during festivals. Recently, rap and hip-hop have become more common too. Music taste is changing, but pop is still number one.

part3.text: Do you think music is beneficial to children?
part3.answer: Yes, music is very good for children. It helps them relax and improves their creativity. Singing or playing music also builds confidence. In addition, music brings joy, which is important for a happy childhood. So I believe music is very beneficial.

part3.text: What are the benefits of children learning a musical instrument?
part3.answer: Learning an instrument trains patience and discipline. Children need to practice every day, which teaches them good habits. It also improves memory and coordination. Most importantly, it gives them a way to express emotions. These skills are useful in many parts of life.

part3.text: Should students have physical education and do sports at school?
part3.answer: Absolutely, it's essential. Physical education teaches students the importance of maintaining an active lifestyle, which is crucial for their long-term physical and mental health. Furthermore, it fosters vital soft skills such as teamwork, perseverance, and sportsmanship, which are applicable far beyond the sports field.

part3.text: What qualities should an athlete have?
part3.answer: Beyond raw physical talent, top athletes must possess immense mental toughness to handle pressure and overcome setbacks. Discipline is fundamental for rigorous training, and a strong work ethic ensures they continuously strive to improve and reach their peak performance.

part3.text: Is talent important in sports?
part3.answer: Talent provides a natural advantage and can be the initial spark for success. However, it is not sufficient on its own. Ultimately, hard work, dedicated practice, and strategic coaching are far more critical factors that determine an athlete's long-term achievement and ability to perform consistently.

topics.answer: The successful sportsperson I truly admire is the tennis champion, Li Na. She was a trailblazer for tennis in China and across Asia. Her greatest achievement was winning the French Open in 2011, which made her the first Grand Slam singles champion from Asia. What I admire most is not just her powerful baseline play but her mental fortitude. She famously had a fierce and independent personality, often using witty humour in her post-match interviews. Her success was groundbreaking because she paved the way for a new generation of athletes, showing that it was possible to compete and win at the highest level on a global stage. She transcended her sport and became a huge inspiration for young people everywhere to be confident and determined.

topics.answer: The creative person I truly admire is the Japanese animator and filmmaker, Hayao Miyazaki. What I find most inspiring about him is his incredible imagination and his meticulous attention to detail. His films aren’t just cartoons; they are profound works of art that explore complex themes like environmentalism, pacifism, and the innocence of childhood. He hand-draws thousands of frames, which is a testament to his dedication and old-school craftsmanship. Furthermore, his strong female characters are particularly admirable, as they are often brave and independent. His creativity has not only entertained millions but also delivered powerful messages that resonate across cultures.

part3.text: Should all scenic spot charge any entry fee?
part3.answer: I don’t think it’s a one-size-fits-all rule—some scenic spots, like small local parks, should be free so everyone can enjoy them, but bigger places with lots of maintenance needs (like ancient temples or national parks) ought to charge a reasonable fee. That fee can go towards fixing paths, protecting wildlife, or hiring staff to keep the place clean, which helps the spot stay nice for future visitors. If every spot was either totally free or too expensive, it might either ruin the place from overuse or shut out people who can’t afford it—so a middle ground makes the most sense.

part3.text: Is visiting the scenic spot the best choice for us while traveling?
part3.answer: I don’t think visiting scenic spots is always the best choice—while they’re often beautiful, traveling’s also about diving into local life, like trying street food or chatting with locals, which can be just as memorable. For example, I once skipped a crowded mountain scenic spot to wander a small town’s markets, and that ended up being the highlight of my trip because it felt more real, not just a “check-the-box” activity. It really depends on what you want: if you love nature or history, scenic spots are great, but if you crave authentic experiences, there are way more options that can be just as good.

part3.text: Why do some people like to live in big cities?
part3.answer: I think a big reason some people love big cities is the huge range of job opportunities—there are way more roles in fields like tech, finance, or media, which lets people chase their career goals easier than in small towns. Another draw is the variety of lifestyle options: you can try different cuisines every weekend, catch a concert on a weekday, or visit museums whenever you want, so there’s never a dull moment. Plus, big cities usually have better public transport and top-notch facilities like hospitals or universities, which makes daily life more convenient and gives people peace of mind.

topics.answer: I’ll describe an interesting building from a trip to Barcelona, using B2-level English with an oral style and idiomatic expressions. The response will cover all required points in 5 sentences.Last summer, I saw the Sagrada Família when I traveled to Barcelona, Spain—it’s right in the heart of the city, so you can’t miss it even from a few blocks away. Its exterior is totally one-of-a-kind: covered in intricate stone carvings of religious scenes, with spires that twist up like giant, detailed tree trunks, and the colors from the stained-glass windows glow beautifully in the sun. I learned from a local guide that it’s been under construction for over 140 years, designed by the famous architect Gaudí, and it’s still not finished yet—they say it’ll be done by 2026. What makes it so interesting is that it blends nature-inspired designs with religious symbolism perfectly; every corner feels like a work of art, not just a regular church, and standing in front of it gives you that “wow” factor you don’t get from most buildings. I could’ve stared at its details for hours—you notice something new every time you look, which is why it stuck in my mind long after the trip.

Others may focus more on human needs and pay less attention to animals, so awareness really makes a difference.

part3.text: Do you think it's important to take children to the zoo to see animal?
part3.answer: Yes, I think it’s important, but in a balanced way. Zoos can help children learn about animals and develop empathy for them. At the same time, children should also be taught about protecting wildlife in their natural habitats, so they grow up with both knowledge and respect for nature.

topics.answer: One wild animal I really want to know more about is the snow leopard. I first saw it in a documentary a few years ago, and I was amazed by how beautiful and mysterious it looked. The snow leopard usually lives high up in the mountains, so it’s very rare to see one in real life. What interests me most is how it survives in such cold and harsh conditions, moving so quietly and blending into the rocks. I’d like to learn more about its habits, diet, and how people are trying to protect it. For me, the snow leopard represents strength and mystery, and I think learning about it would be really inspiring.

part3.text: How do adverts influence children?
part3.answer: Adverts influence children mainly by shaping their preferences and creating a sense of desire. Kids are easily attracted by colorful images and catchy songs, so they quickly want the products they see on TV or online. This can affect their spending habits and even put pressure on parents. At the same time, positive adverts can also encourage healthy behavior, like eating better food or reading more.

part3.text: Should advertising aimed at kids be prohibited?
part3.answer: I think it shouldn ’ t be completely prohibited, but it does need strict regulation. Children are too young to understand the persuasive techniques behind adverts, so they can be easily misled. Instead of banning, governments should set clear rules, like limiting junk food ads and encouraging educational content. This way, advertising can still exist but in a healthier and more balanced form.

part3.text: What’s the difference between the toys kids play now and those they played in the past?
part3.answer: The main difference is that toys today are more digital and interactive, like video games or smart robots. In the past, children played with simpler toys such as dolls, wooden blocks, or skipping ropes. Modern toys may help kids learn technology faster, but traditional ones encouraged more imagination and physical activity. Both types have value, but the balance between them has definitely shifted.

topics.answer: When I was a child, my favorite toy was a set of Lego bricks. My parents gave it to me on my birthday, and I was super excited when I opened the box. part3.text: Is it possible for us to know that children who are 3 or 4 years old will become musicians and painters when they grow up?
part3.answer: It is possible to see some early signs, like when children sing well or love painting. But it’s hard to be sure, because interests can change as they grow. Parents can notice talents, but the future still depends on training, effort, and opportunities.

part3.text: Do you think artists with talents should focus on their talents?
part3.answer: Yes, I think artists with talents should focus on them, but they also need to work hard. Talent gives them a good start, but without practice, they may not succeed. Focusing on their talent can help them create better works and achieve their goals.

part3.text: Why do people like to watch talent shows?
part3.answer: People enjoy talent shows because they are exciting and surprising. They can see ordinary people doing amazing things. Talent shows also give hope and inspiration, showing that anyone can shine if they try. Viewers feel happy and motivated when they watch them.

topics.answer: I want to talk about my talent for drawing. Since I was a child, I have enjoyed using pencils and colors to create pictures. I discovered this talent when I was about seven years old. My teacher asked the class to draw a picture of our family, and mine was chosen to hang on the classroom wall. That moment made me feel proud and confident. Although I like drawing, I never had professional training. I can draw simple things like flowers, houses, and people, but I want to improve my skills. part3.text: What habits should children have?
part3.answer: Children should have habits like reading, exercising, and keeping things tidy. These habits make them healthy, smart, and responsible. For example, daily reading improves knowledge, and regular exercise keeps them strong. Good habits shape their future.

part3.text: What should parents do to teach their children good habits?
part3.answer: Parents should be good role models. If they show healthy habits, children will copy them. They should also give praise when children follow good habits. In addition, setting clear rules at home helps children learn discipline.

part3.text: Why do some habits change when people get older, and how do people change their habits?
part3.answer: Habits change because lifestyle and responsibilities change. For example, students may stop playing games when they start working. People change habits by setting goals and practicing step by step. Motivation and patience are very important for success.

topics.answer: I want to talk about my friend Mark, who has the habit of reading every night before bed. I first noticed this habit when we traveled together last year. Before sleeping, while I was checking my phone, he was quietly reading a book. This habit impressed me because it shows self-discipline. Instead of wasting time on social media, he uses that time to learn something new. He told me that even twenty minutes of reading each night adds up to several books a year. I want to develop this habit because I think reading can improve my knowledge, vocabulary, and even my writing skills. It also helps me relax and sleep better. Compared with watching videos, reading makes me feel more calm and focused. To develop this habit, I plan to put a book on my bedside table and set a fixed reading time. I will start with short books or articles, so I don’t feel too tired. Slowly, I hope reading before bed will become part of my daily routine. This habit seems small, but it can bring big changes. It will not only help me learn but also make my lifestyle healthier and more balanced. I really want to follow his example.

part3.text: Why do people enjoy trying exciting or adventurous activities?
part3.answer: People are drawn to these activities for the adrenaline rush and the sense of living in the moment. It offers a powerful escape from daily routines and provides a tremendous sense of personal achievement. Ultimately, it pushes personal boundaries and makes people feel truly alive and empowered.

part3.text: What should people consider before trying a new adventurous activity?
part3.answer: The most crucial factor is safety. One must ensure they use proper equipment and receive instruction from a certified professional. It's also wise to honestly assess your own physical fitness and health conditions to ensure you can participate without undue risk.

part3.text: How do such activities benefit people personally?
part3.answer: These experiences build mental resilience by teaching individuals to manage fear and stress. They often boost self-confidence and foster a more positive, can-do attitude. Furthermore, the stories and memories created become a source of great joy and social sharing for years to come.

topics.answer: An incredibly exciting activity I tried for the first time was indoor skydiving. It was at a special facility with a large vertical wind tunnel that simulates the freefall sensation of actual skydiving. I was quite apprehensive at first, feeling a knot of nervousness in my stomach as I put on the helmet and flight suit. However, the moment I leaned into the powerful column of air and was lifted off my feet, my fear instantly turned into pure exhilaration. The instructor was very supportive, guiding my body posture to help me stabilize and even perform simple maneuvers. The feeling of weightlessness, of floating effortlessly on a cushion of air, was utterly surreal and liberating. It was an absolute adrenaline rush that left me feeling ecstatic and incredibly proud of myself for conquering my initial fear.

part3.text: Why do some children not like learning science at school?
part3.answer: Some children find science intimidating because it can seem overly abstract and complex. If the teaching relies heavily on rote memorization of formulas and theories without practical experiments, it can quickly become tedious and difficult to grasp, stripping away the natural curiosity and fun of discovery.

part3.text: Is it important to study science at school?
part3.answer: Absolutely, it's fundamental. Science education cultivates critical thinking and problem-solving skills, teaching students how to analyze evidence and draw logical conclusions. It also provides essential knowledge about how the world works, from the human body to the environment, which is crucial for making informed decisions in life.

part3.text: Which science subject is the most important for children to learn?
part3.answer: It's difficult to single one out as each discipline offers unique value. However, a strong case can be made for biology. It is highly relatable as it directly explains their own bodies, health, and the living world around them, fostering an early appreciation for life sciences and personal well-being.

topics.answer: An area of science that has always fascinated me is astronomy. I find it utterly captivating because it deals with the immense scale of the universe, from stars and planets to galaxies and black holes. What intrigues me most is how it explores fundamental questions about our origins and place in the cosmos. For instance, the concept of the Big Bang theory, which explains the beginning of the universe, is both mind-boggling and profound. I often watch documentaries about new discoveries, like exoplanets that might have conditions suitable for life. I think astronomy is humbling; it puts our daily lives into perspective and reminds us that we are part of something vastly larger and more mysterious. It’s a field that is constantly evolving with new, breathtaking discoveries.

part3.text: What kinds of stories do children like?
part3.answer: Children are typically drawn to imaginative and adventurous tales. They love stories with clear heroes and villains, magical elements, talking animals, and exciting quests. Fairy tales, fables, and funny stories with repetitive and rhyming phrases are particularly appealing as they are engaging and easy to follow.

part3.text: What the benefits of bedtime stories for children?
part3.answer: Bedtime stories offer immense benefits. They significantly boost language acquisition and vocabulary. Furthermore, this ritual stimulates a child's imagination and creativity. Crucially, it provides a sense of security and serves as a wonderful bonding opportunity, strengthening the emotional connection between parent and child before sleep.

part3.text: Why do most children like listening to stories before bedtime?
part3.answer: It provides a comforting and predictable routine that helps them wind down from the day's activities. The soothing sound of a parent's voice makes them feel safe and loved. Ultimately, it's a special, focused time that offers undivided attention, making them feel cherished and easing the transition into sleep.

topics.answer: I’d like to describe the traditional Chinese story of Chang’e, the Moon Goddess. It’ s a famous legend often associated with the Mid-Autumn Festival. The tale revolves around a heroic archer named Hou Yi, who shot down nine of ten suns to save the earth from scorching. As a reward, he was given an elixir of immortality. However, his treacherous apprentice tried to steal it. To protect it, Hou Yi’s wife, Chang’e, swallowed the potion herself. She then became immortal but began to float towards the moon, where she was forced to reside alone forever. The story is deeply poignant, exploring themes of sacrifice, love, and loneliness. It’s said that on the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival, the moon is at its brightest and most beautiful, which is when Hou Yi makes offerings to his beloved wife.

part3.text: Do people prefer to eat out at restaurants or eat at home during the Spring Festivals?
part3.answer: While eating out is becoming more popular for convenience, the overwhelming majority still prefer to eat at home. The Spring Festival is fundamentally about family reunion. part3.text: Why do people like to have meals together during important festivals?
part3.answer: Sharing a meal is a profound act of cultural and emotional significance. It reinforces family bonds and a sense of belonging. The food itself is often symbolic, representing wishes for good fortune, health, and prosperity, making the shared experience a way to celebrate heritage and hope for the future together.

topics.answer: The most memorable dinner I can recall was a farewell meal with my closest university friends right after our graduation. We chose a bustling hotpot restaurant, which felt perfectly symbolic of our vibrant and communal friendship. The round table was laden with plates of thinly sliced meat, fresh vegetables, and all kinds of noodles. The real highlight, however, wasn't just the delicious, simmering broth but the atmosphere of shared nostalgia. We spent hours cooking food in the same pot, laughing over inside jokes from the past four years, and making promises to stay in touch. It was a bittersweet celebration, marking the end of an era but also the beginning of our new journeys. That dinner wasn't merely about eating; it was a profound experience of connection and cherished memories.

part3.text: How important is after-sales service for a business?

part3.text: Why do some people not like shopping in small shops?

part3.text: What do people normally plan in their daily lives?
part3.answer: In most cases, people plan basic tasks such as work schedules, study goals, and family responsibilities. Many also arrange their daily meals, exercise routines, and even leisure activities like watching TV or meeting friends. Planning helps individuals stay organized and avoid wasting time on unimportant matters. Nowadays, with mobile apps and digital calendars, people tend to plan more carefully, setting reminders for meetings or deadlines. I believe the extent of planning depends on one’s lifestyle. For example, students may plan around exams, while working professionals often prioritize projects and appointments. Overall, daily planning gives people a clearer direction and greater control over their routines.

part3.text: Is time management very important in our daily lives?
part3.answer: Yes, I think time management is extremely important because it directly affects both efficiency and well-being. When people manage their time wisely, they can complete their work on schedule and still have enough time to relax or spend with their families. Without good time management, individuals may experience stress, miss deadlines, or fail to achieve long-term goals. In today’s fast-paced society, where distractions are everywhere, being able to allocate time effectively is a valuable life skill. It not only improves productivity but also helps people maintain a healthy balance between work, study, and personal life.

part3.text: Do you think it is good to change jobs frequently?
part3.answer: Personally, I don’t think changing jobs too often is a good idea. On one hand, it might give people more exposure to different industries and allow them to develop new skills. However, frequent job changes may also suggest a lack of commitment, which can make employers hesitate to trust them with long-term responsibilities. In addition, switching jobs repeatedly may interrupt career development and prevent someone from gaining deeper expertise in one field. Of course, if a job offers no growth opportunities or has an unhealthy environment, changing positions could be necessary. But overall, stability usually benefits professional growth more than constant movement.

topics.answer: A positive change I’ve made recently in my daily routine is waking up earlier. In the past, I usually got up around 8 or even later, which often left me rushing to start work or lessons. A few weeks ago, I decided to set my alarm for 6:30 every morning. At first, it was quite difficult, but I slowly adjusted by going to bed earlier and avoiding my phone at night. Now, I use the extra time in the morning to do some light exercise, prepare a healthy breakfast, and read for about 20 minutes before starting the day. I think it’s a positive change because it makes me feel more energetic and productive. Instead of starting the day in a hurry, I can begin calmly and with focus. This small change has improved my mood and helped me stay motivated throughout the day.

part3.text: What do you think of the people who waste water?
part3.answer: I think people who waste water are often unaware of the long-term consequences of their actions. Freshwater is a limited resource, and irresponsible use can contribute to shortages, especially in regions already facing drought. In my view, wasting water reflects a lack of environmental awareness and social responsibility. Instead of treating water as endless, individuals should cultivate sustainable habits, such as recycling grey water or installing efficient appliances. Governments and schools also need to raise public awareness about this issue.

part3.text: What are the advantages of water transportation?
part3.answer: Water transportation has several notable advantages, especially for international trade. Firstly, it allows the movement of large quantities of goods at relatively low cost, which makes it highly efficient for bulk commodities like oil, coal, and grain. Secondly, ships can travel across oceans, linking distant markets and promoting global economic integration. Another benefit is that water routes often have fewer physical barriers compared to land transport. Although it can be slower than air travel, its affordability and capacity make it indispensable in today’s economy.

part3.text: Do you think it is good to teach swimming in schools?
part3.answer: Yes, I strongly believe swimming should be taught in schools. On a practical level, swimming is a life-saving skill that can reduce the risk of drowning, particularly in areas near rivers or the sea. Beyond safety, it also contributes to students’ physical health, since swimming improves endurance, strength, and flexibility. Moreover, learning to swim can boost confidence, as children overcome initial fear of water. Schools provide an ideal setting because trained instructors can ensure safety and equal access. Overall, swimming lessons bring both physical and psychological benefits.

topics.answer: A water sport I would really like to try in the future is surfing. I have seen many videos of people riding waves, and it always looks both exciting and challenging. If I had the chance, I would love to try it on a beach in Hainan, since it is famous in China for beautiful seaside views and good surfing conditions. From what I know, surfing is not easy because it requires balance, strength, and quick reactions. Beginners often fall off the board many times before they manage to stand up properly. Even though it looks tough, I think it would be very rewarding to finally catch a wave and enjoy the feeling of moving with the ocean. I would like to try surfing because it seems like a great way to stay active, experience nature, and also push myself out of my comfort zone.

part3.text: Sometimes people should tell lies. Do you agree?
part3.answer: I do agree that there are times when telling lies is necessary—like when you want to spare someone’s feelings, such as not saying a friend’s new haircut looks bad if they’re really happy with it. Those small, kind lies (often called “white lies”) don’t hurt anyone and can keep relationships from unnecessary tension, which is way better than being brutally honest just to “tell the truth.”

part3.text: How do you know when others are telling lies?
part3.answer: I usually tell when someone’s lying by their body language—like if they avoid making eye contact, fidget with their hands, or pause a lot before answering, which often gives them away. Sometimes their words don’t add up either, like contradicting something they said earlier, and that little inconsistency makes me think they’re not being truthful.

topics.answer: I want to talk about a time I told my close friend Lily an important truth. A few months ago, she was considering taking a part-time job that she thought was perfect, but I’d heard from a mutual acquaintance the company often delayed paying wages—so I knew I had to be honest with her. At first, she looked a bit surprised and even a little upset, like she didn’t want to believe it, but after I showed her some small proofs I’d found, she calmed down and thanked me for not letting her walk into a problem. I thought it was important to tell her because she’s someone I care about deeply, and letting her make a decision based on lies would’ve only led to frustration later—honesty’s the foundation of our friendship, after all.

topics.title: Describe a time when you get lost.

cue.title: Describe a time when you get lost.

part3.text: Why do some people get lost more easily than others?
part3.answer: I think some people get lost more easily because they’re not good at paying attention to landmarks—like they might walk past a big statue or a unique shop without noticing, so they can’t retrace their steps later. Others might have a weaker sense of direction, meaning they struggle to tell left from right in new places or don’t pick up on little clues, like which way the sun is shining, that help you stay on track.

part3.text: Do you think it is important to be able to read a map?
part3.answer: I definitely think it’s important to be able to read a map—especially when you’re in a place with no phone signal or where GPS fails, like remote countryside or old city alleys, because it stops you from panicking if you get turned around. Even if you usually use apps, knowing how to read a physical map is a useful backup skill that can save you a lot of time and hassle when tech lets you down.

topics.answer: I’ll talk about a time I got lost while traveling in a small coastal town in southern China last summer. I’d wandered off from the main street to explore a quiet alley filled with old shops, but when I turned back, all the narrow lanes looked identical, and I couldn’t find my way to the hotel. At first, I felt a bit flustered—my phone had no signal, so I couldn’t use maps, and I was worried I’d miss the dinner reservation I’d made. Luckily, I spotted an elderly local sitting outside a teahouse; I explained my situation, and he was kind enough to walk me to the main road, pointing out a big red sign that marked the direction to my hotel. That experience taught me to always note down landmarks when I’m in an unfamiliar place!

topics.title: Describe a trip you would like to make again.

cue.title: Describe a trip you would like to make again.

part3.text: Why do people like travelling?
part3.answer: People enjoy travelling because it gives them a chance to relax, explore new cultures, and see beautiful places. Travelling also helps people learn more about the world and sometimes even about themselves. It’s a way to take a break from routine life and experience something fresh and exciting.

part3.text: What would happen if no preparation were made before the trip?
part3.answer: If no preparation is made, the trip can easily turn stressful. People might face problems like missing documents, running out of money, or not finding transportation. Planning ahead usually makes travel smoother and safer, so without it, the whole experience could become frustrating instead of enjoyable.

part3.text: Why do some people prefer to travel in their own country rather than going aboard?
part3.answer: Some people prefer domestic travel because it feels more convenient and less expensive. They don’t have to worry about language barriers, cultural differences, or complicated procedures like visas. Travelling at home also gives them a chance to appreciate their own culture and discover places they might have overlooked.

topics.answer: A trip I’d love to make again is my visit to Kyoto, Japan, about three years ago. I went there with two of my close friends during the spring, just when the cherry blossoms were blooming. We spent our days walking through old temples, trying different street foods, and taking lots of photos under the sakura trees. The city had a calm and traditional vibe that made me feel like I had traveled back in time. I want to go again because it was one of the most relaxing and beautiful trips I’ve ever had. Sharing that experience with friends made it even more special, and I’d like to relive those memories once more.

topics.title: Describe a long journey you had.

cue.title: Describe a long journey you had.
points: who you had the journey with
and explain how you felt about the journey.

part3.text: What are the advantages of travelling by train on a long journey?
part3.answer: Travelling by train offers a unique advantage: the ability to truly appreciate the landscape. Unlike air travel, you witness the gradual and dramatic changes in scenery, from cities to mountains. It also allows for greater mobility to walk around, making the long duration far more comfortable and social.

part3.text: Why do some people prefer long, slow journeys over fast ones?
part3.answer: Many prefer slow travel as it is not just about the destination but the experience of the journey itself. It allows for deeper immersion and a chance to decompress fully. This pace encourages mindfulness and a stronger connection to the places you pass through, making it more meaningful.

part3.text: What is an important thing to prepare for before a long trip?
part3.answer: Meticulous planning is essential for a smooth trip. This includes thorough research on the climate and culture of your destination to pack appropriately. Crucially, securing all necessary travel documents and bookings well in advance prevents last-minute stress and ensures you can focus on enjoying the experience.

topics.answer: A long journey that stands out in my memory was a cross-country train trip I took with my family from Beijing to Lhasa. The entire journey on the Qinghai-Tibet railway took around 40 hours. The most captivating aspect wasn't the destination itself, but the breathtaking and ever-changing scenery outside the window. We witnessed the dramatic transformation from bustling metropolises and flat plains to the majestic, snow-capped mountains and vast, empty plateaus of Tibet. The highlight was passing by crystal-blue lakes like Namtso, which looked utterly serene. Despite the lengthy duration, it never felt tedious. The cabin was comfortable, and we spent the time chatting, playing cards, and simply gazing in awe at the pristine landscapes. It was a profoundly moving and picturesque experience.

part3.text: Do you think people should apologise for anything wrong they do?
part3.answer: I think people should almost always apologize for things they do wrong— whether it’s a small mistake like bumping into someone or a bigger error, an apology shows you care about the other person’s feelings and takes responsibility for your actions. Skipping an apology can make the other person feel ignored or disrespected, which might turn a tiny issue into something that harms your relationship.

part3.text: Do people in your country like to say “sorry”?
part3.answer: I think people in my country are pretty willing to say “sorry,” especially for small, accidental things like stepping on someone’s foot or being a little late—we see it as a polite way to smooth things over and show respect. For bigger mistakes, though, people might take a bit more time to apologize because they want to make sure their words feel sincere, not just like a quick afterthought.

part3.text: Why do some people refuse to say “sorry” to others?
part3.answer: I think some people refuse to say “sorry” because they mix up apologizing with admitting they’re “fully wrong”—they don’t want to lose face or feel like they’re giving in, even if they know they messed up a little. Others might be too proud to own up to their mistakes, worrying that an apology will make them look weak in front of others, so they’d rather brush the issue under the carpet instead.

topics.title: Describe the first time when you used a foreign language to communicate.

cue.title: Describe the first time when you used a foreign language to communicate.
points: and explain how you felt about the conversation.

part3.text: At what age should children start learning a foreign language?
part3.answer: I think children can start learning a foreign language as early as possible, maybe around three or four years old. At this age, their brains are flexible and they can learn sounds quickly, almost like a game. Of course, it doesn’t need to be very formal. Songs, games, and cartoons are enough in the beginning. Later, when they go to school, they can focus more on grammar and vocabulary. Starting early helps them build confidence and a natural accent, which is harder to achieve when they are older.

part3.text: Does a person still need to learn other languages, if he or she is good at English?
part3.answer: Yes, I believe so. English is important, but other languages also have value. For example, learning Chinese can help people understand one of the world’s biggest markets. French, Spanish, or Arabic are useful in many countries too. Each language opens a door to culture, history, and people’s way of thinking. Even if someone speaks English well, knowing another language can make communication deeper and more personal. It also shows respect to others when you try to speak their language.

part3.text: Do you think minority languages will disappear?
part3.answer: Unfortunately, many minority languages are in danger of disappearing. Globalization and the use of dominant languages like English or Chinese make it harder for small languages to survive. Younger people often prefer to speak the majority language for work and study, so they stop using their native tongue. However, governments and communities can take action. For example, schools can teach minority languages, and local media can use them in programs. I think it’s very important to protect them, because each language carries unique culture and traditions. If a language disappears, part of human history is lost forever.

topics.answer: I still remember the first time I used a foreign language to communicate. It happened about five years ago in Beijing, when I was still in high school. One afternoon, I was walking near a tourist attraction, and a foreign visitor came up to me. He looked a little confused and asked for directions in English. At that moment, I felt both nervous and excited. I had studied English for years in school, but I had never spoken it to a real foreigner before. I took a deep breath and tried to understand what he was saying. Luckily, I caught some key words like “subway” and “station.” I explained in simple English how to walk to the nearest subway station. My sentences were not perfect, but the visitor understood me and thanked me with a big smile. That made me feel really proud. This experience taught me that language is not only about grammar, but also about confidence and communication. I realized that even simple words can help people connect. Since then, I have been more motivated to improve my English, because I know it can open the door to new friendships and opportunities.

topics.title: Describe a time when you saw something interesting on social media.

cue.title: Describe a time when you saw something interesting on social media.
points: and explain why you think it was interesting.

part3.text: Why do people like to use social media?
part3.answer: People like social media because it connects them with others. They can share their lives, see updates from friends, and follow celebrities. It’s also entertaining, with videos, pictures, and stories. Another reason is convenience, because people can get news quickly. Overall, social media gives both information and fun.

part3.text: What kinds of things are popular on social media?
part3.answer: Many things are popular, such as short funny videos, cooking recipes, and travel photos. Young people like fashion tips and music clips, while older people may enjoy health advice. Social media trends change quickly, but entertainment and lifestyle topics are always popular.

part3.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of using social media?
part3.answer: The advantage is that social media helps people stay connected and informed. It’s also a good tool for learning and business. However, it has disadvantages, like spreading fake news or wasting too much time. If people use it carefully, the benefits are greater than the problems.

topics.answer: I remember an interesting moment on social media that happened about six months ago. I was scrolling through my WeChat feed after dinner, just trying to relax. Suddenly, I saw a video that really caught my attention. It was about a young man who used recycled materials to build small houses for stray cats in his neighborhood. The video showed how he collected old boxes, wood, and plastic bottles from the streets. Then he carefully cleaned and designed them into warm, safe houses. The best part was watching the cats happily moving into their new homes. The video was simple, but it was very touching and creative at the same time. I thought it was interesting because it showed how social media can spread positive ideas. Normally, we see funny clips or advertisements, but this video carried a strong message about kindness and creativity. It inspired me to think that even small actions can make a big difference in society. After watching it, I shared the video with my friends, and many of them were impressed too. Some even said they wanted to try similar projects in their own neighborhoods. This made me realize that social media is not only for entertainment but also for education and social change.

topics.title: Describe a time when you broke something.

cue.title: Describe a time when you broke something.

part3.text: What kinds of things are more likely to be broken by people at home?
part3.answer: Everyday items are most frequently broken. This commonly includes fragile tableware like plates and glasses, which can easily slip from one's hand. Electronic devices, such as smartphone screens, also often get damaged from accidental drops. Simple furniture can also break during assembly or moving.

part3.text: What kinds of people like to fix things by themselves?
part3.answer: Typically, it's pragmatic individuals who are naturally curious and resourceful. They often possess a strong do-it-yourself mentality, enjoying the challenge and the intellectual satisfaction of diagnosing a problem. They are usually very practical and derive great pleasure from the sense of accomplishment and the money saved from repairing something themselves.

part3.text: Do you think clothes produced in a factory are of better quality than those made by hand?
part3.answer: It depends on the context. Mass-produced factory clothes benefit from precision machinery, ensuring consistent stitching and uniform quality. However, handmade garments are often superior in craftsmanship, using finer materials and offering unique, custom-tailored details. They represent artisanal quality rather than industrial uniformity.

topics.answer: I’m going to talk about a rather embarrassing time when I broke my friend’s smartphone. It happened at a birthday party a few years ago. We were all in the garden, and I was enthusiastically trying to take a group photo. As I stepped backwards to fit everyone into the frame, I tripped over a small step and fell. The phone flew out of my hand and landed screen-first on the concrete path. I immediately picked it up, and my heart sank – the screen was completely shattered, with a spiderweb of cracks covering the glass. I was utterly mortified and apologized profusely. My friend was very understanding about the accident, though obviously upset. Of course, I insisted on paying for the screen replacement immediately. It was an unfortunate accident that taught me to be much more aware of my surroundings, especially when holding someone else’s valuable belongings.

topics.title: Describe a time when the electricity suddenly was off.

cue.title: Describe a time when the electricity suddenly was off.
points: what you did during that time
and explain how you felt about it.

part3.text: Which is better, electric bicycles or ordinary bicycles?
part3.answer: Neither is inherently better; it depends entirely on the rider's needs. Ordinary bicycles offer a pure physical workout and are simpler to maintain. Conversely, electric bicycles provide assisted power, making them superior for conquering hills, longer commutes, and allowing riders of different fitness levels to travel together effortlessly.

part3.text: Do you think electric bicycles will replace ordinary bicycles in the future?
part3.answer: It's unlikely they will fully replace them. While e-bikes will undoubtedly become more prevalent for practical urban transport, traditional bicycles will always retain a dedicated user base. They are cherished by cycling purists, fitness enthusiasts, and for their mechanical simplicity, lower cost, and the authentic cycling experience they provide.

part3.text: Which is better, electric cars or petrol cars?
part3.answer: Electric cars are better for the environment, offering zero local emissions and lower running costs. However, petrol cars currently have a longer driving range and a more established refuelling infrastructure. The "better" choice hinges on one's priorities: environmental impact and cost versus convenience for very long journeys.

topics.answer: I vividly remember a time when the electricity went off unexpectedly during a severe thunderstorm one summer evening. Our entire neighborhood was plunged into complete darkness. The first thing we noticed was the abrupt silence—the hum of the refrigerator and the air conditioner just stopped. We fumbled in the drawers to find candles and matches, and their flickering light created long, dancing shadows on the walls. At first, my family and I were a bit disoriented, but soon we decided to make the most of it. We sat together in the living room, telling stories and playing board games by candlelight. Without the distractions of TVs and phones, we ended up having a long, heartfelt conversation. Ironically, this inconvenient blackout turned into a wonderfully memorable and bonding experience for us. `

topics.title: Describe a talk you gave to a group of people.

cue.title: Describe a talk you gave to a group of people.
points: who you gave the talk to

part3.text: What are the benefits does the internet bring to communication?
part3.answer: The internet makes communication faster and more convenient. People can connect instantly through messages, video calls, or social media, no matter where they are. It also allows us to share ideas widely and reach a larger audience. Of course, sometimes online communication lacks a personal touch, but overall it has made staying in touch much easier.

part3.text: Which one is better, being a communicator or a listener?
part3.answer: I think being a good listener is slightly more important. Listening carefully helps us understand others’ needs and respond in the right way, which actually makes communication more effective. Without listening, even the best communicator might miss the point. So, in my view, listening is the foundation of real communication.

part3.text: What qualities does a person need to have to be a good communicator?
part3.answer: A good communicator should be clear, confident, and empathetic. Clarity helps others understand the message easily, while confidence makes people trust what you say. Empathy is also crucial, because it allows you to connect with others’ feelings and adjust your tone. Together, these qualities create effective and meaningful communication.

topics.answer: Last year, I gave a short talk to my classmates during an English lesson. The teacher asked us to prepare a small presentation, and I chose to talk about my favorite hobby, playing tennis. I wanted to share it because sports really help me stay active and release stress. At first, I felt a bit nervous standing in front of everyone, but once I started speaking, I felt more confident. My classmates listened carefully and even asked me some questions afterward, which made me feel proud. It was a simple talk, but I enjoyed the chance to express myself in front of a group.

topics.title: Describe a time when you waited for something special.

cue.title: Describe a time when you waited for something special.
points: and explain why it was special.

part3.text: Why do we need to be patient?
part3.answer: Patience is crucial because it allows us to navigate challenges and delays without becoming overwhelmed by frustration or making impulsive decisions. It fosters better judgment, reduces stress, and often leads to more favourable outcomes, as rushing can result in mistakes or missed opportunities.

part3.text: In what situations do we need to be more patient?
part3.answer: We need exceptional patience in situations involving long-term goals, such as studying for a major exam or learning a complex new skill. It's also vital in interpersonal relationships, when resolving conflicts or trying to understand another person's perspective, and during tedious processes like bureaucratic paperwork.

part3.text: Do you think we should be patient all the time?
part3.answer: Not necessarily. While patience is generally a virtue, there are moments where swift, decisive action is required, such as in an emergency or when seizing a fleeting opportunity. Blind patience can sometimes lead to passivity or accepting unsatisfactory conditions when change is possible.

topics.answer: The most memorable time I waited for something special was for the release of my university admission results. The waiting period felt like an eternity, lasting nearly two months after the national entrance exam. To manage my anxiety, I tried to keep myself occupied. I took up a part-time job at a café and spent a lot of time reading novels and watching movies to distract myself. I also frequently chatted with my classmates, who were in the same nervous predicament, which made me feel less alone. This wait was profoundly special because my entire future academic path hinged on that single result. It represented the culmination of twelve years of hard work and was a pivotal moment that would determine the direction of my life. The immense relief and joy I felt when I finally received the offer made the long, agonizing wait completely worthwhile.

topics.title: Describe an important decision you made with the help of other people.

cue.title: Describe an important decision you made with the help of other people.
