part3.text: When do children begin to comprehend the value of money?
part3.answer: Generally speaking, children start to understand the value of money around the age of six or seven, when they’re first given pocket money. If parents explain that money is earned and not unlimited, kids gradually learn how to spend wisely and differentiate between needs and wants. It also helps if they’re encouraged to make small choices with their own money.

part3.text: Should parents reward children with money?
part3.answer: That depends on the situation, but in general, rewarding kids with money for good behavior or completed tasks can teach them about financial responsibility. However, if it’s overused, children might start doing things only for the money and not because it’s right. So, while it can be useful, it should be combined with other types of positive reinforcement.

part3.text: Do you think it's a good thing that more people are using digital payment?
part3.answer: Yes, I think it’s a great development because cashless payments make everyday life smoother and more efficient. They reduce the risk of theft, simplify transactions, and make it easier to track spending. However, people should still be aware of online security risks and over-spending, especially when everything is just one tap away.

topics.answer: One time I received money as a gift was on my 18th birthday, which is considered a big milestone in Chinese culture. It happened two years ago during a small family dinner, and my uncle, who has always supported me, gave me a red envelope with 1000 yuan inside. He told me that since I was about to step into adulthood, I should use the money in a way that would help me grow. At first, I was tempted to spend it on clothes or a meal out with friends, but after thinking it through, I chose to sign up for an online speaking course. It had live sessions with native speakers and really helped me become more confident. What made the gift truly meaningful wasn’t the amount, but the fact that he trusted me to use it wisely. I felt a strong sense of responsibility and wanted to live up to the trust he placed in me. Looking back, I’m still grateful, because it pushed me to invest in something that had long-term value.

part3.text: What bad behaviour do children usually have?
part3.answer: Children sometimes misbehave by talking back to adults, refusing to follow rules, or throwing tantrums when they don’t get their way. Some also act out in public places, like shouting or running around where they shouldn’t. These behaviours are often a way for them to get attention or test limits.

part3.text: How should parents stop their children from behaving badly in public?
part3.answer: Parents should stay calm and try to talk to their child in a firm but gentle way to help them settle down. It’s important to set clear rules and follow through with consequences if the child keeps acting out. Sometimes, taking the child aside for a quiet talk can work wonders.

part3.text: Are parents these days stricter than those in the past?
part3.answer: I think parents these days are generally less strict than in the past because many focus more on open communication and understanding. In the past, children were expected to follow rules without question, but now parents tend to give them more freedom. That said, some still lay down the law when it comes to discipline.

topics.answer: I remember seeing a child behave badly in a shopping mall a few months ago. He was throwing a tantrum in the middle of a toy store because his parents refused to buy him a toy he wanted. He screamed at the top of his lungs, kicked the shelves, and even knocked some items onto the floor. Most of the shoppers looked quite uncomfortable, and a few walked away quickly to avoid the scene. The parents looked embarrassed but didn’t really do much to calm him down. Honestly, I felt a bit annoyed but also sorry for the parents—it’s not easy to deal with that in public. It made me think about how important it is to set clear boundaries for children.

part3.text: How should children spend their allowance money?
part3.answer: Ideally, they should learn to split their money between spending, saving, and maybe even giving. This teaches them basic money management and helps them understand value over time.

part3.text: Why do people like shopping more now than in the past?
part3.answer: Mainly because it’s easier and more fun now. With online shopping, you can browse thousands of items without leaving your home. Plus, shopping has become a way for many people to unwind after a stressful day.

part3.text: Do you think shopping is good for a country's economy?
part3.answer: Definitely—it boosts demand, supports businesses, and creates jobs. But if people overconsume, it can also lead to waste and environmental damage. So, it’s about finding a balance.

topics.answer: The unforgettable gift I received was a Jay Chou concert ticket from my best friend. I had been talking about the concert for weeks, but when the tickets were released, they were sold out in less than a minute. I was disappointed, but I didn’t expect anything after that. A week later, my best friend handed me the gift during lunch—she had somehow managed to get a ticket and kept it a secret. I was so shocked and touched, not just because I got to see my favorite singer live, but because I felt seen and understood without even asking for it. That concert had been on my bucket list for years, and the fact that she made it happen meant the world to me. Moments like this really show that small gestures can mean a lot, especially when they come from someone who knows you well.

part3.text: What do people in your country often do while waiting?
part3.answer: People commonly use their phones to browse social media or play games while waiting. Many read books or listen to music to pass the time. Some simply observe their surroundings or strike up conversations with others nearby.

part3.text: Why do some people like a slow-paced life?
part3.answer: Some prefer a slow-paced life because it reduces stress and allows for better work-life balance. It gives them more time to enjoy hobbies and personal relationships. This lifestyle often leads to greater mindfulness and appreciation of daily moments.

part3.text: Is being patient good for people?
part3.answer: Patience helps people make more thoughtful decisions and maintain better relationships. It enables individuals to persevere through challenges without frustration. Developing patience often leads to greater personal and professional success.

topics.answer: A memorable time I chose to wait was during my university graduation job hunt last year. After receiving an okay job offer in March, I decided to hold out for better opportunities aligned with my career goals. I waited specifically for a sustainability consultancy role I'd interviewed for, which had a longer hiring process but matched my passion for environmental work. Though anxious about finances, I declined the first offer because the company had poor growth prospects. The 2-month wait was nerve-wracking, especially when friends secured jobs. To cope, I networked and upskilled in carbon accounting. When the dream offer finally came, the relief and pride validated my patience. This experience taught me that strategic waiting, though stressful, can lead to more fulfilling outcomes.

part3.text: Is punctuality important to people?
part3.answer: Punctuality is generally valued as it shows respect for others' time and reflects professionalism. part3.text: What do you think is a good way to record things?
part3.answer: The most effective method combines digital tools like calendar apps with handwritten notes. Setting multiple reminders (phone alerts + physical planners) ensures important items aren't missed. Color- coding and prioritization systems help organize different types of appointments.

part3.text: Which is more important, a work-related appointment or an appointment with a friend?
part3.answer: Importance depends on context - critical work meetings may take precedence, but consistently prioritizing work over personal commitments can harm relationships. The ideal approach is balancing both through proper scheduling and communication when conflicts arise.

topics.answer: Last month, I completely missed my dental check-up scheduled for 2pm on a Tuesday. It was an important six-month cleaning appointment that I'd made with Dr. Chen at Sunshine Dental Clinic three weeks earlier. The reason I forgot was pure schedule overload - I had back-to-back work meetings that morning and failed to set a reminder. What made it worse was that I'd even written it in my planner, but got so absorbed in preparing a presentation that I didn't check my schedule after lunch. When the clinic called to ask why I hadn't shown up, I was mortified. After apologizing profusely, I had to pay a no-show fee and wait another three weeks for a new appointment. This experience taught me to always set multiple reminders for important commitments.

part3.text: Should people set goals for themselves?
part3.answer: Yes, goal-setting provides direction and motivation. Clear objectives help measure progress and maintain focus. However, goals should be realistic to avoid frustration. People who set achievable targets tend to accomplish more while staying motivated.

part3.text: How would you define success?
part3.answer: Success means achieving personal fulfillment, not just material gains. It involves growth, balance, and positive impact. True success aligns with one’s values and brings lasting satisfaction rather than temporary rewards.

part3.text: How can we judge whether young people are successful nowadays?
part3.answer: Modern success includes adaptability, emotional intelligence, and purpose. Beyond income, growth mindset and community contributions matter. Young people thriving in these areas demonstrate true achievement.

part3.text: What kinds of customer service do you think is good?
part3.answer: Well, in my opinion, good customer service should be efficient, polite, and solution-focused. For example, if there’s a product issue, staff should respond quickly and offer a clear solution rather than making excuses. What really matters is whether customers feel respected and taken care of, even if the product itself has a problem.

part3.text: What problems do customers often have while shopping?
part3.answer: I think the most common problems include wrong deliveries, damaged goods, or misleading product descriptions. These issues are especially common in online shopping. Sometimes, poor customer service also makes things worse when customers try to fix the issue.

part3.text: What do you think of people complaining when they buy poor quality goods at a low price?
part3.answer: To be honest, if something is dirt cheap, it’s a bit unrealistic to expect top-notch quality. However, sellers still need to deliver what they promised, even if the price is low. I think it’s totally fair to complain if the product is totally unusable or if the description was misleading. But complaining just for the sake of it doesn’t really help anyone.

topics.answer: Well, one shopping experience that didn’t go smoothly happened about six months ago when I bought a pair of sneakers from an online store. It was a limited-edition release from a local brand that I had been following for months, and I was super excited when I finally managed to place an order. However, the problem started right after I received the package. First of all, the size was completely wrong—I ordered a size 42, but they sent me a 40. On top of that, one of the shoes had a visible scratch on the side, which really disappointed me. Since I bought it during a big sale, the customer service was extremely slow to respond, and I had to email them several times before they agreed to process a return. To be honest, I felt really frustrated because I had been looking forward to wearing those shoes, especially since they were not cheap. But at the same time, the experience taught me to always double-check the details and read reviews before buying from a brand I haven’t tried before. In the end, I did get a refund, but the whole thing left a bad impression.

part3.text: Why is plastic waste a serious problem in modern society?
part3.answer: Plastic waste is a big problem because it takes hundreds of years to break down. It causes pollution in the land, rivers, and oceans. Animals may eat plastic by mistake and get sick or die. Also, plastic waste is everywhere, and it’s hard to clean up. It makes cities and nature dirty and unhealthy.

part3.text: How does plastic waste affect the environment differently in cities and rural areas?
part3.answer: In cities, plastic waste often blocks drains and causes flooding during rain. It also makes the streets look dirty. In rural areas, it can harm animals or get burned, which creates air pollution. Cities may have better waste systems, but in the countryside, it’s harder to manage plastic waste properly.

part3.text: Do you think single-use plastics (e.g., bags, straws) should be banned completely? Why or why not?
part3.answer: Yes, I think single-use plastics should be banned because they are used only once but pollute the environment for years. There are many better options now, like paper bags or reusable straws. If we don’t stop using them, plastic will continue to hurt nature and animals.

topics.answer: Last summer, I went to a beach near my hometown with some friends. We were excited to swim and enjoy the sunshine. But when we got there, we saw a lot of plastic waste all over the sand. There were plastic bottles, food wrappers, broken plastic chairs, and even some old plastic bags floating in the water. It was really shocking. Some kids were playing nearby, and I felt sad because the place was not safe or clean anymore. We picked up some of the trash, but there was too much for just a few people to handle. I felt angry and disappointed that people didn’t care about nature. It made me realize how serious the plastic pollution problem is. I also decided to join a local beach clean-up group later that month.
